claims.text: The claim asserts that because total current-dollar PCE rose in April 2024 ($39.1 billion, 0.2 percent), both goods and services spending must have risen.

citations.quotation: personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $39.1 billion (0.2 percent).

counterarguments.text: Real (chained-dollar) goods PCE decreased 0.4 percent in April while services increased 0.1 percent, showing the goods component did not rise in quantity terms. However, these are chained-dollar measures, not current-dollar measures, so they do not directly refute the claim about current-dollar values; they only show the claim's implied quantity logic fails and that the aggregate increase could have been driven by prices or by services.

citations.quotation: Real DPI decreased 0.1 percent in April and real PCE decreased 0.1 percent; goods decreased 0.4 percent and services increased 0.1 percent (tables 3 and 4).

counterarguments.text: The monthly percent-change table also shows chained-dollar goods moving differently from the aggregate: Goods -0.2 percent versus PCE 0.2 percent in April, indicating the components did not move together and the aggregate rise does not establish that goods spending rose.

limitations: The excerpts do not include current-dollar (nominal) monthly percent changes or dollar levels for goods and services separately for April 2024; only total current-dollar PCE (+$39.1 billion, +0.2 percent) is given, so the goods and services contributions in current dollars cannot be quantified from the supplied text.

The provided goods (-0.4 percent) and services (+0.1 percent) figures are real/chained-dollar changes, and the source notes 'Chained-dollar values are not additive because the relative weights for a given period differ from those of the reference year,' so they cannot be summed to decompose the current-dollar aggregate.
Percent changes calculated from chained-dollar levels may differ from index changes due to rounding, per the source.
Excerpts are partial; Tables 2 and 3 (which would contain current-dollar detail by product) are not fully reproduced, and compressed PDF table columns may be misread.
The April 2024 figures are preliminary/revised estimates published 2024-05-31; the publication date is declared, not independently verified.
